lead.headline: Rescue resumes on Nepal-Tibet border as flood toll passes 630
lead.dek: Nearly 3,000 people are missing after crews paused for a day while an unstable barrier lake overflowed
body: Rescue crews in Nepal and Tibet went back to work Saturday after pausing while a newly formed barrier lake at the disaster site overflowed, with Nepal's police counting 626 dead and Chinese authorities at least seven more across the border. Nepal's disaster authority lists 2,426 people missing on its side, 517 of them foreign tourists and workers, and Chinese officials report 554 missing in Tibet.

The disaster began Wednesday morning when a glacier collapsed at roughly 5,200 meters and plunged 1,200 meters into the Lende River valley, sending a surge that raised the Trishuli River nine meters in half an hour through Rasuwa, Nuwakot and Dhading districts and Tibet's Gyirong county. The U.S. State Department has said about 90 Americans were impacted, many of them pilgrims bound for Mount Kailash; no American deaths have been confirmed.

Glacial scientist Alton Byers said the debris dam holding back the new lake is highly unstable and that the safest outcome would be a natural, gradual drainage. Aid has arrived from India, the U.N., the Red Cross federation, Australia, South Korea and the United States, and Nepal has asked for specialist help including tunnel rescue teams.

briefs.headline: Trump announces deal taking majority stake in Venezuelan oil
briefs.summary: The agreement negotiated with acting President Delcy Rodriguez gives a new private company 100-year rights to 65 billion barrels across 17 fields, with the U.S. taking 55% of effective output; gas averages $4.09 a gallon amid the Iran war.

briefs.headline: Judge blocks Postal Service rule restricting mail-in ballots
briefs.summary: U.S. District Judge Indira Talwani issued a 14-day restraining order Thursday against the USPS rule requiring state voter lists and barcoded envelopes, citing a risk of "pervasive disenfranchisement"; a Sept. 3 hearing follows.

briefs.headline: Hochul pardons deported Purple Heart veteran Sae Joon Park
briefs.summary: New York's governor erased the drug and bail-jumping convictions of the Panama invasion veteran who self-deported to South Korea in 2025; his lawyers can now ask the immigration appeals board to vacate his removal order.

briefs.headline: Trump orders Lake Ontario renamed Lake America
briefs.summary: Thursday's executive order, effective immediately for federal usage, follows 50% tariffs on $20 billion in Canadian goods; the U.S. cannot compel other countries to adopt the name, as with last year's Gulf of America order.

briefs.headline: Norway's crown prince takes the throne as King Haakon VIII
briefs.summary: Haakon announced his regnal name after his father Harald V died Friday at 89; a motor procession carried the late king from the hospital to the royal palace, and national mourning runs until a funeral date is set.

briefs.headline: Treasury moves to cut Egyptian bank's UAE arm from the dollar
briefs.summary: The named-bank sanction Scott Bessent promised by week's end landed Friday on Banque Misr's Emirati branches, with a proposed rule severing their U.S. correspondent access; OFAC also designated Bank Melli's Dubai branch manager.

briefs.headline: Haitians demand answers from police over Kenscoff massacre
briefs.summary: Authorities opened an investigation into whether complicity or negligence let gangs kill 47 people and abduct more than 50 on Aug. 23; a gang leader's video threatens the hostages, and police will not discuss rescue plans.

briefs.headline: Nigeria sends specialist team after mosque mass abduction
briefs.summary: Police chief Tunji Disu deployed a rescue force with military and intelligence units to Borgu, where gunmen seized more than 60 worshippers from mosques near the Benin border; Catholic bishops decried the attacks.

briefs.headline: State closes Ohio County Correctional Center immediately
briefs.summary: The Division of Corrections announced Friday it is shutting the Wheeling facility and moving its 54 low-security inmates to other prisons within 30 days; Commissioner David Kelly said no jobs are being eliminated.

briefs.headline: Four flood-hit counties get SNAP hot-food waiver
briefs.summary: USDA approval Friday lets SNAP recipients in Lewis, Pleasants, Ritchie and Upshur counties buy hot prepared foods through late September, a response to the July 21-22 storms behind the federal disaster declaration.

briefs.headline: Bluefield State board fires President Darrin Martin
briefs.summary: Governors voted Thursday to void the contract they renewed in July, citing at least $1.5 million in unpaid obligations, a missed $7 million state appropriation request and unreported NCAA issues; Cathy Deeb is acting president.

briefs.headline: Martinsburg cleans up from 5.5 inches of rain in an hour
briefs.summary: City manager Andy Blake called Thursday evening's downpour a thousand-year storm by NOAA's tables; Martinsburg High and two elementary schools closed Friday with water intrusion and crews worked through the night on the streets.

regional.item: The fire marshal swapped eviction notices for do-not-enter signs at six reclassified buildings, though the cited fire-code violations remain unfixed.
Austin Gessel agreed to take the Kanawha County Commission seat Lance Wheeler vacated, with a swearing-in set for Tuesday.

away.item: A federal PFOA class action filed Tuesday seeks municipal water hookups and medical monitoring for Bennington and Shaftsbury.

hotspots.item: Pender County's school board met Wednesday on renovation plans for Topsail Middle in Hampstead, after the new J.H. Lea K-8 shifted the district's footprint.

briefs.headline: Election sign season opens ahead of Prince George's civic vote
briefs.summary: Campaign signs can go up from Tuesday at 14 designated city locations for the Oct. 17 municipal election, under bylaws specific enough to diagram how many faces a sign may carry; they come down within three days of the vote.

briefs.headline: Two more MLAs quit B.C. Conservatives over Findlay's conduct
briefs.summary: Brennan Day and Teresa Wat walked Wednesday, the fourth and fifth caucus exits since Kerry-Lynne Findlay won the leadership in May; Wat cited unanswered accusations about her loyalty to Canada.

briefs.headline: Carney rejects Lake Ontario rename as tariff fight deepens
briefs.summary: The prime minister said the name predates both Confederation and the Declaration of Independence and will stand; Ottawa's counter-tariffs of 15% to 50% on $20 billion in U.S. goods take effect Sept. 8.

briefs.headline: Experimental eye drops restore light perception in blind mice
briefs.summary: Light-switchable compounds called prosthe6, from a consortium led by Barcelona's IBEC and published in JACS, stood in for lost photoreceptors in models of macular degeneration; the researchers stress they do not cure the underlying disease.

briefs.headline: Curiosity marks a kilometer of climbing with a 323-frame panorama
briefs.summary: The rover passed 1,000 meters of elevation gain Wednesday in its 14th year on Mars, and its Mastcam view from Valle Grande looks back downslope to Gale Crater's floor with its own tracks receding into the haze.

briefs.headline: Clearest image yet of Betelgeuse's century-suspected companion
briefs.summary: ESO's Very Large Telescope caught Betelgeuse B at maximum separation, and the team led by Miguel Montarges reports in Astronomy & Astrophysics that it is two to three solar masses - big enough to help explain the supergiant's pulsing.

briefs.headline: Roman telescope cleared for a 7:26 a.m. Sunday launch
briefs.summary: NASA and SpaceX finished the readiness review Friday for the Falcon Heavy flight from Kennedy's pad 39A, with forecasters giving 60% favorable weather; a backup window opens Monday at 7:22 a.m. ET.

briefs.headline: Judge rules Pentagon blacklisting of Anthropic unlawful
briefs.summary: U.S. District Judge Rita Lin found Thursday that the supply-chain-risk label, imposed after the AI company refused any-lawful-purpose contract terms, was unconstitutional retaliation, and ordered the directives rescinded.

briefs.headline: 100-plus companies warn of a closing window on AI cyberattacks
briefs.summary: An open letter from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Microsoft and banks and security firms says AI-enabled attacks on hospitals and water systems will surge within months, and asks governments to fund defensive AI for essential services.

art.caption: An Armed Police Force rescuer crosses the mud-buried valley floor alone, shovel in hand, past a house filled to its windows with debris.
art.credit: Sketched from an Al Jazeera photograph

weather_ear: The morning forecast lands at 7:15, from Jim Claudtore.
kicker: Parkersburg, Nicholas-Webster and the New River were quiet, and Webster County's half of Vacation Hotspots came up empty a second morning.
